mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5.25% for three consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains above for 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant negative relationship with the FEDFUNDS 3-month moving average (p > 0.05 in OLS).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a strengthening labor market, which boosts investor confidence and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns within 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 10% month-over-month while UNRATE decreases by > 0.2 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: In a robustness check, the correlation between PAYEMS change and UNRATE change is not statistically significant (p > 0.1), or 20-day forward returns are not higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 2% for two consecutive months suggests strengthening supply-side demand, which anticipates a positive S&P 500 5-day forward return.
failure_condition: INDPRO growth does not predict SPX 5-day returns (Granger causality rejected at 5% significance).

mechanism_narrative: When consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) unexpectedly spikes by more than 0.3 percentage points in a month, it triggers a risk premium adjustment that produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not statistically negatively correlated with CPIAUCSL surprise (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the 2-year yield proxy (FEDFUNDS) below 3% for 10 trading days is interpreted as a forward guidance signal for rate cuts, which tends to drive positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS 2-year moving average falls below 3% for 10 consecutive days
failure_condition: No significant positive return in the 60 days following the 10-day FEDFUNDS decline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising job openings (PAYEMS) without a corresponding rise in layoffs suggests a labor market in expansion, which increases equity valuations and supports positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: PAYEMS growth is not predictive of SPX 20-day returns (rolling Granger causality rejected).

mechanism_narrative: When the ratio of industrial production to capacity utilization (INDPRO / HOUST) falls below 0.7 for a month, it indicates underutilized capacity, which often precedes a positive S&P 500 5-day forward return as market prices in recovery.
failure_condition: The ratio remains below 0.7 for more than 3 consecutive months without a significant positive SPX 5-day return (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of persistent monetary tightening (FEDFUNDS rising by > 0.25% per month for 4 months), S&P 500 20-day forward returns tend to be negative due to discounting of future cash flows, unless offset by a simultaneous surge in equity demand proxies.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS monthly change > +0.25% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: In a tightening regime, 20-day forward returns are not significantly different from a baseline of zero (p > 0.05).
